$comment: CreateMessage -> POST /2010-04-01/Accounts/{AccountSid}/Messages.json, form encoded, 201. `To` is the only field the schema requires; a sender is `From` or `MessagingServiceSid`, and content is `Body`, `MediaUrl` or `ContentSid`. 0.1.0 sends text: Body is required here.
title: Send an SMS with Twilio
$idempotencyComment: CreateMessage takes no idempotency key. A retry after a timeout can text the person twice.

config.label: From
config.description: A Twilio number you own, in E.164, or an alphanumeric sender ID where the destination allows one. Give this or a Messaging Service.

config.label: Messaging Service SID
config.description: MG... A Messaging Service picks the sender from its pool. Give this or From.

config.label: Body
config.description: The text. Up to 1,600 characters. A character outside GSM-7 makes the whole message UCS-2, which halves how much fits in each billed segment.

config.label: Status callback URL
config.description: Optional. Twilio POSTs delivery status changes here. Verifying those requests arrives in 0.2.0.

requireOneOf.error: message_send needs a sender: From (a Twilio number) or a Messaging Service SID. Twilio refuses a message with neither.

outputShape.description: queued, sending, sent, delivered, undelivered, failed, scheduled, canceled, and others. A send answers `queued` or `accepted`, not delivered: delivery is reported later.
The sender. Null while a Messaging Service is still choosing one.
How many SMS segments Twilio billed or will bill. A STRING in Twilio's schema.
The Messaging Service used, if any.
Twilio's error code when the message failed, e.g. 21610 (the recipient replied STOP). Null otherwise.
Twilio's description of the error. Null otherwise.
The price, negative, once known. Null until then.
Which estate this ran against: fake or live.
